messages:
Alex Kim: Heads-up — getting capacity signals in us-west-2 (gpu-dedicated). queue depth spiking for p99 workloads, low-priority routes seeing ~30% admission rejects. anyone already looking?
Mira Patel: saw the alert, checking autoscaler + warm-standby pools. CPU/GPU utilization looks normal on nodes, but scheduling backlog on the GPU scheduler is high.
TJ Chen: is this only one model family or broad? any model fallback kicking in?
Alex Kim: mostly long-context and embedding routes. fallback to quantized variants didn't trigger automatically (policy is conservative). capacity-bot: ALERT us-west-2 gpu-dedicated p95_util=96% queued=118 reject_rate=0.31
Sasha Ivanov: can we temporarily increase cross-region spill threshold? the policy is set to 20% but with network egress costs we'd like to be deliberate.
Mira Patel: proposal: flip spill_mode to 'aggressive' for 10m to reduce queue depth, keep per-model token caps in place. This will route to us-east-1 warm standby first, then eu-west if needed.
TJ Chen: agree as short term. but need to halve batch_size for long-context models to reduce token pressure — do we have a knob to change batching per model pool without deploy?
Leo Wang: we can push batching override via runtime config: `PATCH /runtime/config` with body: ```json
{
  "batch_overrides": {"long-context": {"max_batch_tokens": 2048}}
}
```
Mira Patel: doing the config patch now. also enabling spill_mode=aggressive.
capacity-bot: ACTION applied: spill_mode=aggressive -> us-east-1 allowed, per-model caps retained.
Alex Kim: after patch queue depth dropped by ~40% in 2m. p95 latency improved but cost estimate looks higher if we sustain cross-region egress.
Sasha Ivanov: cost tradeoff: short burst vs dropped requests. for SLOs I'd accept spend for 5-15m bursts. we should set a budget guard so it auto-reverts.
Mira Patel: adding transient budget: `budget_window=15m, egress_budget_usd=120` — will auto-revert spill_mode after budget or time.
TJ Chen: we should also tune admission control to prefer model-fallback locally before spilling. i can open a tiny change to routing priority: local_quantized -> local_model -> cross_region_variant.
Alex Kim: that ordering makes sense. can we set fallback threshold to 60% queue depth? avoid spilling for small blips.
Sasha Ivanov: +1. also add metric alert for sustained egress > threshold so cost team gets pinged.
Leo Wang: rolling the routing priority patch now. snippet: ```yaml
routing: 
  tiers:
    - name: local_quantized
      weight: 100
    - name: local_full
      weight: 80
    - name: cross_region
      weight: 50
```
capacity-bot: NOTE: routing config change queued for rollout to us-west-2.
Alex Kim: quick runbook note for oncall: 1) check capacity-bot alerts; 2) if queued>100 and p95_util>92% -> enable aggressive spill for 15m with budget; 3) reduce long-context batch tokens; 4) notify cost oncall.
Mira Patel: wrote runbook snippet into the incident doc. linking here: https://redwood/internal/runbooks/spillover-mitigation (private)
Sasha Ivanov: final question — do we want to keep per-customer (tenant) throttles tighter during spill? we saw heavy tenants consuming most of queue.
TJ Chen: yes, ramp tenant-level rate_limit multiplier down to 0.6 for non-sla tenants as an automated step in the runbook.
Leo Wang: done — tenant multipliers config applied.
capacity-bot: RESOLVED alert for us-west-2 (queued dropped to 27). historical note: peak queued 130 -> mitigated by routing + batch overrides.
Alex Kim: good job team. follow-ups: TJ to PR routing priority change, Sasha to add cost alerting, Mira to bake budget guard into control plane. closing thread. :thumbsup:
